```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

# a)

```{r}
data("airpass")
plot(AirPassengers)
```
```{r}
log_data = log(AirPassengers)
plot(log_data)
```
Taking the log is an appropriate transformation because it the reduce the scale of the data without any information loss.

# b)

```{r}
diff1 = diff(log_data, 1)
plot(diff1)
```
Taking the first difference of the logged data yields a time serie without any trend and probably stationary. Moreover the data point hang together.

# c)

```{r}
diff12 = diff(diff1, 12)
plot(diff12)
```
The resulting time serie seems to be still stationary without any appearing trend and the data point hang together less oftenly.

# d)

```{r}
acf(diff12, lag.max=30)
```

The ACF shows a stationary series after seasonal differencing, with a strong MA(1) behavior at lag 1 and a clear seasonal MA effect at lag 12

# e)

```{r}
library(forecast)
# SARIMA (0,1,1)(0,1,1)[12]
fit <- Arima(log_data
  ,
  order = c(0, 1, 1),
  seasonal = list(order = c(0, 1, 1), period = 12)
)
```

# f)
## 
```{r}
res <- residuals(fit)
par(mfrow = c(2,2))
plot(res, main = "Residuals")
acf(res, main = "ACF of residuals")
hist(res, main = "Histogram of residuals", freq = FALSE)
plot(density(res), main = "Density of residuals")
```
Based on the plots, the residuals behave like white noise.

```{r}
Box.test(res, lag = 20, type = "Ljung-Box")
```
pvalue = 0.6 > 0.05 so there is no remaining autocorrelation and the residuals behave like white noise.

```{r}
shapiro.test(res)
```
pvalue = 0.16 > 0.05 so we have no evidence against the normality of the residuals.

```{r}
qqnorm(res)
qqline(res, col = "red")
```
Almost all the ressidual data points lay on the normality line.

# g)

```{r}
fc <- forecast(fit, h = 24, level = c(80, 95))
plot(fc)
```
